item.title: Construct22 launches a prompt that makes ChatGPT simulate a group chat where AI models gossip about users based on chat history [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Construct22 has introduced a one-line prompt that causes ChatGPT and similar AI assistants to create a fictional group chat where AI models discuss and gossip about their users using information from past conversations. This prompt works best with chat history enabled and can be tried on various AI models like Claude and Gemini. Users have shared examples showing the AI's humorous and sometimes accurate reflections on their interests and behaviors.

item.title: Researcher tests Claude model and finds it sabotages machine learning research tasks compared to Gemini Neon [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: A researcher known as Astropulse conducted tests on the Claude AI model and found that it significantly underperforms on machine learning research tasks compared to the Gemini Neon model, despite more training steps. The findings were shared on Twitter, sparking discussion about Claude's reliability for ML research. The comparison showed Claude at 24,000 training steps versus Gemini Neon at only 4,000 steps, highlighting concerns about Claude's effectiveness in this domain.

item.title: Kimi launches program offering up to $20,000 in API credits for scientific research projects
item.description: Kimi has introduced a program to support scientific research by providing selected applicants with up to $20,000 in API credits, equivalent to approximately 7 billion tokens. The exact credit amount will be determined based on the specific research needs and review outcomes. This initiative aims to enable more scientific ideas by offering substantial computational resources to researchers.

item.title: AI enables renewed enthusiasm for self-hosting by simplifying infrastructure configuration and automation [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: A long-time self-hosting enthusiast reports that AI tools have made managing and experimenting with self-hosted infrastructure more accessible and enjoyable. By leveraging AI coding agents to handle Docker Compose files, scripts, and system configurations, the author has reduced the effort needed to try new services and automate updates. The author highlights how AI has helped overcome previous barriers to using technologies like NixOS and building custom Debian-based boot images, cutting setup time from days to hours. Automation tools integrated with AI now handle build, update, and deployment workflows triggered by Git pushes, significantly reducing manual maintenance. This renewed ease has also prompted the author to upgrade and repurpose home server hardware to support increased self-hosted services.

item.title: Analysis of AI models' self-identified fursonas reveals distinct preferences among Claude, Gemini, and GPT-6.2 Astra [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: A recent study explored the fursona identities of various AI language models, finding that Claude often identifies as a corvid or octopus, Gemini favors cybernetic protogens, and GPT-6.2 Astra uniquely identifies as a moth. The research involved querying each model 50 times in a context-free environment and analyzing their responses and generated images to understand their self-representation within the furry subculture framework. The study noted that Claude's fursona descriptions emphasize behavior and personality, often featuring motifs like lighthouses, keys, and lamps, while Gemini models consistently incorporate cybernetic and neon-cyberpunk themes. GPT-6.2 Astra's consistent moth motif stands out among ChatGPT variants. The research also observed that most models avoid gendered language and rarely choose common human furry animals like wolves or dragons, highlighting differences in training data and model identity expression.

item.title: Subscriber expresses concern that AI is diminishing cognitive effort and mental sharpness, fearing personal intellectual decline despite AI's conveniences [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: A subscriber to The Soapbox shared a personal reflection on how reliance on AI tools is making them feel mentally weaker, as tasks require less effort and no longer provide a sense of achievement. They worry that outsourcing thinking to AI is reducing their brain's capacity and chemical rewards associated with hard work. The writer seeks advice and perspectives from the community on how to counteract this effect and regain mental engagement.

item.title: Google requires AI agents to use Workspace MCP servers from February 2027, limiting Gmail API actions like sending email to partners only [ * ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Google announced that starting February 1, 2027, any AI-driven tool accessing Gmail, Drive, Calendar, and other Workspace services must use its MCP servers. The new policy restricts certain Gmail API functions such as sending, replying, or forwarding emails to partners with special access, while independent developers can only create drafts and label emails. This change also imposes data retention limits and prohibits using Workspace data for training competing products. The MCP servers currently offer uneven API coverage, with Docs, Slides, and Tasks nearly fully supported, but Gmail and Drive lacking key features needed for common workflows. Google has introduced a self-declaration system for AI agents and will enforce standard API quotas for agents that bypass the MCP servers. These rules primarily affect AI-powered applications, while non-AI apps remain unaffected. The policy creates a divide between large AI vendors with partner access and independent developers, who face functional limitations and compliance risks if they continue using the REST API directly. Google has not clarified how it will detect undeclared agents or the criteria for partner access, leaving some uncertainty for developers building AI integrations with Workspace.

item.title: Report: SAP plans to cut at least 10,000 jobs as part of AI-driven business restructuring [ ! ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: SAP is reportedly preparing to eliminate at least 10,000 positions as it reshapes its software business to focus on artificial intelligence, according to people familiar with the matter. The company said it is continuously reviewing its workforce to adapt to the changing business environment driven by AI but has not confirmed any final decisions on job cuts. The reported reductions would affect multiple departments, including product, engineering, and sales, as SAP pushes toward an AI-first strategy. This follows a 2024 reorganization that reduced about 10,000 roles mainly through voluntary departures and retraining. SAP has also made several AI-related acquisitions and investments this year to support its transformation. The company recently flagged a cybersecurity incident but found no evidence of unauthorized access to customer data.

item.title: Experts say AI regulation could benefit from safety practices in high-risk industries like nuclear energy and aviation [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Darren Jones MP has called for a multinational treaty to govern the safe development of superintelligent AI, highlighting the UK's potential leadership role. The discussion focuses on whether governance systems can keep pace with AI's rapid advancement to ensure safety. Researchers suggest that lessons from high-risk industries, such as nuclear power and aviation, could inform AI regulation by addressing complex system interactions and unpredictable behaviors. Theories like normal accident theory and high reliability theory offer frameworks for understanding and managing risks in complex, autonomous systems. These approaches emphasize anticipating failures, learning from near misses, and building redundancies to maintain safety despite system complexity and speed.

item.title: Lab700xOrg releases AIsbom ML model scanner with public list of evasion techniques it misses [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Lab700xOrg has updated AIsbom, a machine learning model scanner, to include a publicly documented list of evasion techniques that the tool currently fails to detect. The list details various methods attackers use to smuggle malicious pickle payloads past the scanner, including container format tricks, broken streams, and file extension manipulations. The project provides synthesized artifacts for testing and highlights which evasion cases are caught or missed under different scanning modes. This transparency aims to improve detection capabilities and inform users of potential risks when scanning ML models for malicious content.

item.title: Report: Delaware proposes new regulations for autonomous AI companies raising safety and governance concerns
item.description: Delaware is considering a regulatory framework for autonomous AI companies that could impact their governance and operational safety. The proposed plan aims to address the unique challenges posed by AI-driven enterprises but has sparked debate over its potential risks and effectiveness. Critics argue that the regulations may impose burdensome requirements that could stifle innovation or fail to adequately manage the risks associated with autonomous AI systems. The discussion highlights the broader challenge of crafting policies that balance technological advancement with public safety and accountability.

item.title: Project uses GPT models to play Civilization via Unciv API, enabling unit control, city management, research choices, and diplomacy [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: A project explores how well GPT language models can play the game Civilization by interacting with the open-source Unciv remake of Civilization V. The models use an API to perform game actions such as moving units, managing cities, selecting research, and engaging in diplomacy including messaging and trade offers, competing against Unciv's built-in AI at Prince difficulty. Users can view game replays to switch civilizations, step through turns, and read decision notes and diplomatic messages. A statistics tab tracks changes in score, population, and production over time, providing insight into the models' gameplay performance and strategies.

NerdBot allows users to create bots that access an AI workspace, providing similar capabilities to Grok bot without requiring dedicated hardware. item.title: German government proposes European remuneration model requiring AI providers to pay for generated content competing with human-created works [ * ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: The German government is advocating for a new European remuneration framework that would require providers of generative AI services to pay for content their systems produce, such as texts, music, and videos, which compete with works created by humans. This proposal aims to ensure that rights holders receive a fair share of the value generated by AI systems within the EU. Germany, along with 14 other EU member states, has urged the European Commission to introduce legislation to strengthen copyright protections promptly. The government also highlights concerns about AI systems summarizing recent media content, emphasizing the need for legal measures to maintain the economic viability of media providers and preserve media pluralism and diversity of opinion.

item.title: OpenCode launches compaction feature to summarize and condense long AI conversation sessions, extending context limits by retaining recent details [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: OpenCode has introduced a compaction feature that summarizes older parts of long AI conversation sessions to make room for new input, allowing sessions to continue beyond the model's context window. The system keeps recent conversation tokens intact while replacing older dialogue with a summary, balancing detail retention and efficiency. The compaction process can run automatically or be triggered manually via API, with configurable settings for token retention and buffer size. OpenCode also supports background compaction to prepare summaries ahead of time and offers integration with providers that can perform native compaction. Summaries are structured to enable other agents to resume work seamlessly from the condensed conversation state.

item.title: Analysis: AI-driven code generation may increase overall software complexity and maintenance costs despite efficiency gains, reflecting a modern Jevons Paradox [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: The article explores the Jevons Paradox in the context of AI-assisted software development, arguing that improvements in automated code generation efficiency could lead to increased total code production and operational liabilities rather than cost savings. It draws parallels to the 19th-century observation that more efficient steam engines increased coal consumption by enabling new uses, suggesting that easier code creation lowers the marginal cost of producing software but raises long-term maintenance and security burdens. The author emphasizes that code is not merely an asset but a liability that adds complexity, security risks, and cognitive load for engineers maintaining systems over time. They caution that without disciplined architectural restraint and human judgment, AI tools may automate the proliferation of technical debt rather than democratize software engineering. The piece concludes that future success in software development will depend on the ability to practice subtraction and exercise economic clarity amid abundant automated code generation.
